title: Million-dollar HDB resale flats and affordability measures
asked: He asked whether the Ministry is concerned that million-dollar HDB resale transactions surged by 54.7% to 1,594 units in 2025 while overall price growth moderated to 2.9%, and what measures the Government is considering to moderate such transactions and safeguard public confidence in public housing affordability.
response: Mr Chee Hong Tat said resale flat prices are set by the open market at prices agreed between buyers and sellers, depending on the flat's location and attributes. In 2025, about 6% of resale flats transacted above $1 million, and the resale market continues to provide a wide range of flats at different price points. He cited 4-room resale flats with leases of 70 years or longer in Tampines and Punggol at around $650,000 to $700,000, in Sembawang and Yishun below $600,000, and in Jurong West and Woodlands below $550,000, with housing grants of up to $230,000 for eligible first-time resale buyers. He said the Q1 2026 flash estimate showed resale prices declined slightly by 0.1%, and expected moderation due to robust BTO supply and more flats finishing MOP entering the resale market from 2026, with further increases in 2027 and 2028.

left_open: Specific measures to moderate million-dollar resale transactions themselves.
How public confidence in public housing affordability will be safeguarded.
Whether the income ceiling review examines households exceeding the ceiling being pushed into the resale market and contributing to price inflation there.
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered MOP flats in mature estates and the BTO income ceiling review.
